Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 92, verse 1:

﴿By the night when it covers﴾ with its darkness everything between the heaven and the earth.

﴿By the day when it reveals itself﴾: it became clear and manifest.

*Idha* (إذا) in both places is merely for time (*al-zarfiyya*, the adverbial sense of time), and the element that governs it is the verb of oath.

ﷺ

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 92, verse 3:

﴿Wa-mā﴾ (and what / and He who) is in the sense of "man" (who), or it is a verbal noun (maṣdariyya). ﴿khalaqa al-dhakara wa-l-unthā﴾ (created the male and the female): Adam and Eve, and every male and every female. As for the khunthā (hermaphrodite, one of uncertain sex) who is ambiguous to us, he is male or female in the sight of God Most High; so if someone swears not to speak to a male or a female, he breaks his oath by speaking to him.
Indeed, your striving (﴿سَعْيَكُمْ﴾), i.e., your deeds, is ﴿diverse (لَشَتَّى)﴾, i.e., varied: one who works for Paradise through obedience, and one who works for the Fire through disobedience.
﴿As for he who gives﴾ [the due right of] Allah ﴿and fears﴾ Allah

Translation of the Jalalayn gloss on verse 92:6:

﴿And affirms the best (al-husna)﴾, i.e., "There is no god but Allah," in both places.
﴿So We will make it easy for the ease﴾ — for Paradise.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 92, verse 8:

﴿But as for he who is stingy﴾ with regard to the right of Allah ﴿and considers himself self-sufficient﴾ regarding His reward.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 92, verse 10:

﴿So We will ease him toward the difficult﴾ We shall prepare him ﴿for the difficult﴾ for the Fire.
﴿وما﴾ is a negating particle (*nafiyya*). ﴿His wealth will not avail him when he falls (*taraddā*) into the Fire.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 92, verse 12:

﴿Indeed, upon Us is guidance.﴾ (It is) to make clear the path of guidance from the path of misguidance, so that Our command to follow the first is obeyed and Our prohibition against committing the second is heeded.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 92, verse 13:

﴿And indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the first (life).﴾ I.e., the worldly life. So whoever seeks both of them from other than Us has erred.

﴿So I have warned you﴾, meaning I have frightened you, O people of Makkah, ﴿of a Fire blazing﴾. The word تَلَظّى (talaẓẓā) is read with one of the two taʾs (التّاءَيْن) deleted from its original form, but it has also been recited with both retained, meaning it is blazing fiercely.

"Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 92, verse 15:

﴿None shall enter it﴾ (yaṣlāhā, i.e. yadkhuluhā) ﴿except the most wretched﴾ (al-ashqā), in the sense of al-shaqiyy (the wretched one).

﴿Who denied﴾ the Prophet, ﴿and turned away﴾ from faith. This restriction is to be interpreted (ta'wil) in light of His saying: "And He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills." So the intended meaning is the one who will burn (al-Salli) perpetually (al-Mu'abbad).

The text: "﴿وسَيُجَنَّبُها﴾ يُبْعَد عَنْها ﴿الأَتْقى﴾ بِمَعْنى التَّقِيّ"

Translation:

﴿And the most righteous will be kept far from it﴾ (yubʿadu ʿanhā) is kept far from it; ﴿the most righteous﴾ (al-atqā) in the sense of al-taqī (the one who is God-fearing).

﴿Who gives his wealth to purify himself﴾, seeking purification in the sight of Allah the Exalted, by giving it for the sake of Allah the Exalted, not for show (riya' [showing off]) or for reputation (sum'a [seeking to be heard of]), so that he becomes pure in the sight of Allah. This was revealed concerning al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, when he bought Bilal, who was tortured for his faith, and freed him. The disbelievers said: "He only did that because of a favor Bilal had done for him, so it was repaid." Then this was revealed: ﴿And no one has a favor with him that is repaid﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 92, verse 20:

﴿Except﴾ but he does that ﴿seeking the face of his Lord, the Most High﴾, i.e., seeking the reward of Allah.

﴿And he will surely be satisfied﴾ with what he is given of reward in Paradise. The verse includes whoever does the like of his deed. Allah the Exalted is pleased with him, so he is kept far from the Fire and rewarded.
